text:
Running a production database on a 2 GB VPS sounds like a bad idea, and it's also some of the most fun I've had with Postgres. Here's what it took to get good performance out of very small hardware.

We started out optimistic, with `shared_buffers` set to 512 MB because a big cache seemed like an obvious win. It wasn't. We got three OOM kills in the first month. The Linux kernel doesn't negotiate, and a memory budget has to cover every connection, every worker, and every background process.

What fixed it was PgBouncer. Pooling connections cut our active connections from 200 to 20. The server settled down, latency dropped, and the small VPS handled far more than we expected.

This post covers what we learned, the mistakes we made, and the tuning that took a shaky setup to a stable one.
